<section class="section-block" aria-labelledby="research-title">

<div class="section-intro compact-intro">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Current research</p>
<h2 id="research-title">A primary project and a related interest</h2>
</div>
<p class="intro-copy">My main doctoral interest is the political economy of infrastructure finance in lower-income economies. A second, earlier-stage interest builds on my background in machine learning and labour-market research.</p>
</div>
<div class="research-overview">
<article class="research-card primary-interest">
<p class="project-kicker">Proposed doctoral project</p>
<h3>Infrastructure finance in Malawi’s energy sector</h3>
<p class="stream-question">When governments and development institutions support privately financed infrastructure, who bears the fiscal and foreign-exchange risks, and what control do public actors retain over investment and service provision?</p>
<p>I am developing a public-source comparison of financing arrangements in Malawi’s energy sector. The initial cases include the operational Salima and Golomoti solar projects and the proposed Mpatamanga hydropower project.</p>
<a class="text-link" href="research.html#doctoral-project">Project and design</a>
</article>
<article class="research-card secondary-interest">
<p class="project-kicker">Developing research interest</p>
<h3>AI adoption, firms, and work</h3>
<p>I am interested in which firms adopt AI in lower-income economies, which complementary capabilities shape use, and how adoption changes tasks and workplace authority.</p>
<p>This is an early research direction rather than a completed paper.</p>
<a class="text-link" href="research.html#ai-interest">Current feasibility work</a>
</article>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<h2 id="experience-title">What I have worked on</h2>
</div>
<p class="intro-copy">My experience includes linked administrative data and programme evaluation at the OECD, randomised news experiments and research software at NHH, quantitative modelling at EIT Oxford, and large-scale OCR/NLP data construction at NBER.</p>
</div>
<div class="experience-grid">
<div class="experience-item">
<h3>Empirical research</h3>
<p>Applied econometrics, matching, experiments, panel data, and linked administrative records.</p>
</div>
<div class="experience-item">
<h3>Models and measurement</h3>
<p>Life-cycle health and growth models, sensitivity analysis, health-index construction, and heterogeneous-effect analysis.</p>
</div>
<div class="experience-item">
<h3>Research infrastructure</h3>
<p>Python, R, Stata, SQL, OCR/NLP, reproducible pipelines, and open-source experimental tools.</p>
